Kyle — thanks for the quick read and the clear asks. High level, we can offer three structured options for GPU-cost movement that we routinely propose for Reserved Capacity deals; I summarized in the attached spreadsheet but pasted condensed language below so procurement/legal can review quickly.

Option A — Fixed price with quarterly true-up (conservative)
- 12-month committed capacity, fixed per-token price for first 3 months.
- Quarterly true-up based on observed GPU index delta. If GPU market costs increase >8% QoQ, a negotiated true-up is triggered (cap + floor apply).

Option B — Indexation with capped pass-through (recommended for pilot)
- 12-month commit. GPU indexation: per-token rate adjusts with a public GPU-cost index (we propose L2 GPU spot index).
- Pass-through capped at +/-12% over baseline per-token rate; Redwood will absorb any delta between 12% and 22% up to a 10% absorption band for first 6 months to protect trial economics.

Option C — Fixed discount with escalation path (least operational lift)
- Fixed discount off list that automatically adjusts only on explicit agreement by both parties. Any adjustment >15% requires Redwood sales + finance + legal approval.

Recommended commercial mechanics (we suggest B with hybrid cushion):
- 12-month term with the 60-day signature window you requested.
- GPU indexation clause with a 12% cap (pass-through) and a temporary absorption band where Redwood covers incremental costs between 12–22% for the first two quarters.
- Any discount change or concession beyond the absorption band triggers an exec approval path (Sales Director + VP Finance) and requires confirmation within 10 business days.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which option procurement prefers (A/B/C).
2) If B, Laura can draft concrete contract language for the GPU indexation clause and the absorption band.
3) If you need immediate pricing examples for CFO review, the attached spreadsheet has 3 stress scenarios (flat, +15% GPU, +30% GPU).

Let us know which scenario you want to move to term-sheet language — we can also run a 2-week holdback (no signature required) while your finance runs the stress tests.

—Karthik

Team — quick internal note/suggested language and approval path so we can get procurement what they need tomorrow. Copy for legal as well.

Recommended commercial position (final for term sheet):
- Term: 12 months firm from effective date; signature window: 60 days from term-sheet date.
- Pricing mechanic: Hybrid GPU indexation (Option B)
  • Baseline index: Redwood publishes using the publicly verifiable L2-GPU Spot Index (link in doc).
  • Quarterly adjustments: per-token rate adjusts by measured index delta.
  • Pass-through cap: +/-12% of baseline per-token rate.
  • Absorption band: Redwood absorbs the delta between 12% and 22% for the first two quarters only.
  • Cumulative exposure cap: Redwood total absorption liability capped at 8% of total committed fees across the 12-month term (this answers their CFO ask).

Approval & escalation path (for contract/legal):
- Routine adjustments within pass-through cap: handled by Sales Ops (no exec approval).
- Any adjustment requiring Redwood to absorb >22% in a quarter OR request to change discounts >15%: requires Sales Director (Ben Carter) + VP Finance (Monica Patel) approval.
- If exposure would exceed the cumulative cap above, must be escalated to CFO (name on file) for written approval within 10 business days.
